body:
Hi,

I'm an intern at **KUBUDS Tech**, a RISC-V International member organization. I'm very interested in this **KernelCI Statement of Work** and would like to get involved.

I'm relatively new to KernelCI and Linux kernel testing, but I'm highly motivated to learn and contribute. Could you please let me know what the next steps are to participate?

Specifically, I'd like to ask:

- Is this SOW still open and looking for a primary contributor?
- Who should we contact as the mentor or coordinator for this project?
- Is there a recommended onboarding path, or any smaller first tasks suitable for a beginner?
- How should our organization formally engage with the RISC-V Development Partner program for this work?

Thank you very much! I'm looking forward to contributing to the RISC-V ecosystem.

Update (2026-08-22): as an intern at KUBUDS Tech (a RISC-V
International member organization), I ran three fix experiments for the
pointer_masking failure in our guest (kernel v7.2.0-rc7, QEMU -cpu max):

1. Test-side: passing PR_TAGGED_ADDR_ENABLE makes the test SIGSEGV
   (rc=139) - enabling the ABI applies masking to the test process
   itself, so its untagged stack addresses fault.
2. Kernel-side: remembering the rounded PMLEN without touching envcfg
   has no effect - PR_GET derives the effective PMLEN from envcfg.PMM,
   not from mm->context.pmlen.
3. Conclusion: the test's expectation contradicts the kernel's
   documented semantics, so the test itself needs a rewrite (e.g.
   probing via a raw-syscall child). Experiment logs and patches:
   https://github.com/xjysiiau/kernelci-riscv/tree/main/patches

Happy to provide full logs, rerun any of the experiments on request, or
help draft a patch once the intended semantics are confirmed. Thanks
for your time!

Best regards,
X Jys

## Update(2026-08-24): real-hardware (Lichee Pi 3A) validation is now running as the second target

Following up on my earlier comment: we've now got real-hardware validation working alongside the QEMU pipeline described by X Jys above. Same test criteria, real silicon.

Status on real hardware (Lichee Pi 3A / SpacemiT K1, Bianbu 0.6, kernel 6.1.15):

1. cpuinfo ISA detection: PASS (rv64imafdcv_..., Vector present)
2. RVV vector test: PASS on real silicon, VLEN = 256 bits (vs 128 in QEMU)
3. Vector performance baseline: 4M-element add in ~36 ms (stable across runs)
4. Repo: https://github.com/Acidmoon/kernelci-riscv-li3a (scripts, results, regression trend)
5. CI: self-hosted runner drives the board automatically on every push — regression history at results/trend.md

## Known boundaries :

1. K1 has no H (Hypervisor) extension → KVM real-hardware tests impossible on this board; only QEMU-simulated H is available
2. No ZPM → abi/pointer_masking takes the SKIP path here; the upstream mismatch X Jys found only appears on QEMU's simulated ZPM platform (confirmed)
3. Board kernel is 6.1.15 (vendor BSP) → full kselftest run needs a newer kernel; we plan to upgrade the board and run the official selftests side-by-side with the QEMU results
4. We're still very happy to hear from a mentor/coordinator on next steps and the upstream integration path (see the tracking issue at kernelci/kernelci-project#579). 

Thanks!

Excellent and happy to hear!

We are still working out who will lead this, but excited to get you involved.  We have our next Dev Partners meeting tomorrow, and I will make sure to raise that there is interest in this projects.

Thanks and have a great day!
